## Reading an answer out

A model often explains its reasoning before it gives the answer. To read
only the answer, ask the model to put the final answer in a fenced block
with the label `answer`. A fenced block starts with three backticks and
a label on one line, and ends with three backticks on a line of their
own.

`extract_fence(text, tag)` returns the contents of the last block that
has the label `tag`. The default `tag` is `answer`. If the text has no
such block, it returns the whole text with leading and trailing
whitespace removed.

`matches_(actual, expected)` is the simplest grader. It returns `True`
when `actual` contains `expected` as a substring. `expected` can also be
a list of accepted values. The result is `True` when `actual` contains
any of them.

```

*True when `actual` contains `expected`, or any value in a list of
accepted values.*

target="_blank" style="float:right; font-size:smaller">source</a>

### extract_fence

``` python
def extract_fence(
    text, tag:str='answer'
):
```

*The contents of the last fenced block labelled `tag` in `text`, else
the whole stripped text.*

``` python
test_eq(extract_fence('thinking\n```answer\n42\n```'), '42')
test_eq(extract_fence('```answer\nfirst\n```\nand\n```answer\nsecond\n```'), 'second')
test_eq(extract_fence('  just prose  '), 'just prose')      # no fence: the reply is the answer
test_eq(extract_fence('```sql\nSELECT 1\n```', 'sql'), 'SELECT 1')
test_eq(extract_fence(None), '')
```

``` python
test_eq(matches_('the answer is 42', 42), True)
test_eq(matches_('the answer is 42', ['41', '42']), True)   # any accepted value will do
test_eq(matches_('the answer is 42', 43), False)
test_eq(matches_(None, 1), False)
```

## A chat to ask

`_EchoChat` is a test chat. It has no model. Its `_oneshot` returns the
next item of the list `replies` and stores each prompt and system prompt
in `asked`. Its `_structured_call` decodes the next reply as JSON.

The examples below use it to show what each method does with a given
reply. The results do not depend on a real model.

``` python
class _EchoChat(Chat):
    "A chat whose `oneshot` replies from a script, for testing what the helpers do with an answer."
    _runtime, ctx_limit, token_count = 'echo', 8192, 0
    def __init__(self, model=None, *, replies=(), **kw):
        self.replies, self.asked = list(replies), []
        self._setup(model, None)
    def _oneshot(self, prompt, sp='', think=None, max_tokens=None):
        self.asked.append((prompt, sp))
        return self.replies.pop(0) if self.replies else ''
    def _structured_call(self, prompt, schema, sp):
        return json.loads(self._oneshot(prompt, sp))

register_runtime(Runtime('echo', _EchoChat, ('echo-',)))
```

## Classifying

`chat.classify(text, labels)` asks the model to choose one of `labels`
for `text`. It returns one item of `labels`, or the reply text when no
label matches.

<table>
<colgroup>
<col style="width: 50%" />
<col style="width: 50%" />
</colgroup>
<thead>
<tr>
<th>Model reply</th>
<th>Result</th>
</tr>
</thead>
<tbody>
<tr>
<td>Contains a label, in any case:
<code>I think this one is Ham</code></td>
<td>The label as you wrote it in <code>labels</code></td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>Contains several labels</td>
<td>The first of them in the order of <code>labels</code></td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>Contains no label</td>
<td>The reply, in lower case, with whitespace removed from both
ends</td>
</tr>
</tbody>
</table>

The request turns thinking off. A label is found as a substring. The
label `ham` also matches the reply `hamster`.

The example below uses the labels `spam` and `ham`.

### Chat.classify

``` python
def classify(
    text, labels, sp:str='Reply with only the single best label and nothing else.'
):
```

*Ask the model which of `labels` fits `text`, without touching the
conversation.*

``` python
c = _EchoChat(replies=['spam'])
test_eq(c.classify('buy now', ['spam', 'ham']), 'spam')
assert 'spam, ham' in c.asked[0][0]
```

``` python
c = _EchoChat(replies=['I think this one is Ham, personally.'])
test_eq(c.classify('hello', ['spam', 'ham']), 'ham')     # matched loosely, and cased back
c = _EchoChat(replies=['no idea'])
test_eq(c.classify('hello', ['spam', 'ham']), 'no idea') # nothing matched: say so, do not guess
```

## Structured output

`chat.structured(prompt, schema)` asks the model for a JSON object that
matches `schema`. It returns an object of type `schema`. `schema` is
usually a dataclass. It can also be any callable that accepts keyword
arguments.

Each backend implements `_structured_call(prompt, schema, sp)`, which
returns the decoded JSON. A backend can force a tool call, or limit the
output with a grammar. The base
[`Chat`](https://vedicreader.github.io/urai/chat.html#chat) raises
`NotImplementedError`.

`chat.structured` builds its result with `mk_obj(schema, data)`, where
`data` is the decoded JSON that `_structured_call` returns.
[`mk_obj`](https://vedicreader.github.io/urai/eval.html#mk_obj) rebuilds
nested values from the type hints of `schema`. It applies the first row
of this table that fits.

<table>
<colgroup>
<col style="width: 33%" />
<col style="width: 33%" />
<col style="width: 33%" />
</colgroup>
<thead>
<tr>
<th><code>schema</code></th>
<th><code>data</code></th>
<th>Result</th>
</tr>
</thead>
<tbody>
<tr>
<td><code>Optional[X]</code>, or a union of <code>X</code> and
<code>None</code></td>
<td>Any</td>
<td><code>mk_obj(X, data)</code></td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>A union of several types, other than <code>None</code></td>
<td>Any</td>
<td><code>data</code>, unchanged</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td><code>list[X]</code></td>
<td>A list</td>
<td>A list of <code>mk_obj(X, item)</code> for each item</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td><code>tuple[X, ...]</code></td>
<td>A list</td>
<td>A tuple of <code>mk_obj(X, item)</code> for each item</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td><code>tuple[X, Y]</code>, with fixed types</td>
<td>A list</td>
<td>A tuple that pairs each type with the item at the same position</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>Any</td>
<td>Not a dict</td>
<td><code>data</code>, unchanged</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>A dataclass</td>
<td>A dict</td>
<td>A <code>schema</code> object. Nested values are rebuilt with <a
href="https://vedicreader.github.io/urai/eval.html#mk_obj"><code>mk_obj</code></a>,
using the type hints. Keys that are not <code>init</code> fields of the
dataclass are dropped.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>Another callable</td>
<td>A dict</td>
<td><code>schema(**data)</code></td>
</tr>
</tbody>
</table>

A list that does not meet a `list` or `tuple` schema is returned
unchanged, as any other value that is not a dict.

### mk_obj

``` python
def mk_obj(
    schema, d
):
```

*Build `schema` from decoded JSON `d`, rebuilding nested dataclasses.*

``` python
from dataclasses import dataclass

@dataclass
class Addr: city: str; zip: str
@dataclass
class Person: name: str; addr: Addr

p = mk_obj(Person, {'name': 'Ada', 'addr': {'city': 'London', 'zip': 'N1'}})
test_eq(p, Person('Ada', Addr('London', 'N1')))
test_eq(type(p.addr), Addr)              # rebuilt, not left as a dict
```

``` python
@dataclass
class Route: stops: tuple[Addr, ...]; ends: tuple[Addr, int]

r = mk_obj(Route, {'stops': ({'city': 'Rome', 'zip': '1'},), 'ends': ({'city': 'Oslo', 'zip': '2'}, 3)})
test_eq(r, Route((Addr('Rome', '1'),), (Addr('Oslo', '2'), 3)))
r
```

``` python
test_eq(mk_obj(Addr, {'city': 'Rome', 'zip': '00100', 'extra': 'ignored'}), Addr('Rome', '00100'))
test_eq(mk_obj(Person, 'not a dict'), 'not a dict')
test_eq(mk_obj(dict, {'a': 1}), {'a': 1})

@dataclass
class Team: lead: Addr | None; sites: list[Addr]; pair: tuple[Addr, ...] = ()
test_eq(mk_obj(Team, {'lead': {'city': 'Rome', 'zip': '1'}, 'sites': [{'city': 'Oslo', 'zip': '2'}], 'pair': [{'city': 'Bern', 'zip': '3'}]}),
        Team(Addr('Rome', '1'), [Addr('Oslo', '2')], (Addr('Bern', '3'),)))
test_eq(mk_obj(Team, {'lead': None, 'sites': []}), Team(None, []))
```

``` python
c = _EchoChat(replies=['{"city": "Rome", "zip": "00100"}'])
test_eq(c.structured('where?', Addr), Addr('Rome', '00100'))
test_fail(lambda: Chat('echo-1', runtime='echo')._structured_call('x', Addr, ''))
```

## Grading

`chat.check(question, expected)` sends `question` with the system prompt
`qa_sp_`, which asks for a fenced final answer. It reads the answer with
[`extract_fence`](https://vedicreader.github.io/urai/eval.html#extract_fence)
and grades it against `expected`. It returns an `AttrDict` with the keys
`question`, `expected`, `answer` and `ok`. `ok` is the grade.

<table>
<colgroup>
<col style="width: 33%" />
<col style="width: 33%" />
<col style="width: 33%" />
</colgroup>
<thead>
<tr>
<th>Argument</th>
<th>Grader</th>
<th>Extra model request</th>
</tr>
</thead>
<tbody>
<tr>
<td>None (default)</td>
<td><code>grade_fn(answer, expected)</code>, which is <a
href="https://vedicreader.github.io/urai/eval.html#matches_"><code>matches_</code></a>
by default</td>
<td>None</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td><code>grade_fn=f</code></td>
<td>Your function <code>f(answer, expected)</code></td>
<td>None</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td><code>llm_judge=True</code></td>
<td><code>grades</code> on the same chat</td>
<td>One</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td><code>judge=other_chat</code></td>
<td><code>grades</code> on <code>other_chat</code></td>
<td>One, to <code>other_chat</code></td>
</tr>
</tbody>
</table>

`grades(question, expected, actual)` asks the model whether the answer
`actual` is correct, given the reference answer `expected`. It returns
`True` when `classify` selects `yes` from the labels `yes` and `no`. The
matching rules are those of `classify`. A label is found as a substring
of the reply, and the first label wins when the reply holds both. A
reply such as `no, not yes` therefore grades as `True`.

A substring test fails when the answer is `forty-two` and `expected` is
42. A model judge compares the meaning of the two. When you pass
`judge`, a different model grades the answer, and the model that
answered does not grade itself. `llm_judge` and `judge` replace
`grade_fn`.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

<a href="https://github.com/vedicreader/urai/blob/main/urai/eval.py#L80"
target="_blank" style="float:right; font-size:smaller">source</a>

### Chat.check

``` python
def check(
    question, expected, grade_fn:function=matches_, llm_judge:bool=False, judge:NoneType=None, tag:str='answer',
    sp:str='Answer the question, then put your final answer inside a ```answer fence.'
):
```

*Ask `question` without touching the conversation, read the fenced
answer, and grade it against `expected`.*

------------------------------------------------------------------------

<a href="https://github.com/vedicreader/urai/blob/main/urai/eval.py#L72"
target="_blank" style="float:right; font-size:smaller">source</a>

### Chat.grades

``` python
def grades(
    question, expected, actual
):
```

*Ask this chat’s model whether answer `actual` is correct given the
reference `expected`.*

``` python
c = _EchoChat(replies=['Adding them up.\n```answer\n42\n```'])
r = c.check('what is 40+2?', 42)
test_eq((r.answer, r.ok), ('42', True))
test_eq(r.question, 'what is 40+2?')
```

``` python
c = _EchoChat(replies=['```answer\n41\n```'])
test_eq(c.check('what is 40+2?', 42).ok, False)
test_eq(len(c.asked), 1)                 # no second call: substring grading is free
```

``` python
# a judge is a second model call, and can be a different model entirely
answerer = _EchoChat(replies=['```answer\nforty-two\n```'])
judge = _EchoChat(replies=['yes'])
r = answerer.check('what is 40+2?', 42, judge=judge)
test_eq((r.answer, r.ok), ('forty-two', True))   # substring grading would have failed this
test_eq(len(judge.asked), 1)
```

``` python
answerer = _EchoChat(replies=['```answer\nseven\n```'])
test_eq(answerer.check('what is 40+2?', 42, judge=_EchoChat(replies=['no'])).ok, False)
c = _EchoChat(replies=['```answer\n42\n```', 'yes'])
test_eq(c.check('what is 40+2?', 42, llm_judge=True).ok, True)   # judged by itself
```
